U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (1999). U.S. Methane Emissions 1990-2020: Inventories, Projections, and Opportunities for Reductions. EPA 430-R-99-013, Office of Air and Radiation, September 1999.

Region: United States. Locators are PRINTED page numbers (footer style III-9, IV-3, 4-9). Extracted: Exhibit III-5 (best management practices) and III-6 (partner-reported opportunities) for natural gas systems, 27 options with capital, annual O&M and percent reduction; the coal mine cost analysis of Exhibit IV-4 (Options 1 and 2 wells, gas enrichment, compression, gathering, dehydration, water disposal; Option 3 ventilation air oxidiser) with Exhibit 4-7 and 4-8 assumptions and Exhibit IV-3 recovery efficiencies; baseline emission factors from Exhibit III-1 in _other-values. Not extracted: the Exhibit III-7 schedule of 118 options for 2010, Exhibit IV-5 mine-by-mine schedule, the landfill, livestock, manure and other chapters. PRICE YEAR NOT STATED on capital and O&M costs (Exhibit 4-8 prints 1996 US$ only for the base gas price of 2.53 USD/MMBtu); publication year 1999 used with USD. Break-even gas prices are printed in USD/MMBtu and are stored in _other-values. COST BASIS is programme-average national cost per unit (device, facility, compressor, station, well, mile); costs are not per t CH4. The dry-seal O&M is a saving and is stored negative. Option 3 oxidiser derived per MMscf CH4 assumes 8,760 h/yr operation, not printed. Heating-value basis: methane taken at 1,000 Btu/scf as printed in the coal chapter.
